properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 30 at 3:58PM PDT until October 31 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at
02:39 PM Friday 10/30, and 1.5 feet above normal (7.3 ft MLLW)
at 03:44 PM on Saturday 10/31. These predictions include up to
1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 feet above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31, and 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 30 at 2:19PM PDT until November 1 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected for elevations above 7000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to 10 inches, with up to 18 inches at the highest
peaks. Minor accumulations of up to 3 inches possible down to 6000
feet.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 7000 feet, including Highway 50 and
Interstate 80.

* WHEN...From 8 AM PDT Saturday to 7 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels initially 7000 to 8000 feet
Saturday, lowering to 6000 to 7000 feet Saturday night into Sunday.
Heaviest snowfall expected Saturday evening into Sunday. Light
flurries possible down to 5000 feet on Saturday night into Sunday,
but no accumulations expected below 6000 feet.
properties.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.
